title: Leave a finish buffer
hook: One task runs five minutes late. Which appointment absorbs it?

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Distinguish planned slack from overlapping bookings.

objective: Distinguish planned slack from overlapping bookings.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: One task runs five minutes late. Which appointment absorbs it? What keeps five minutes of delay from overlapping the next task? Correct option: A five-minute gap. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.

All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. claims.text: A gap can absorb up to its length of delay in this schedule. It is a stated allowance, not a guarantee about real tasks.

recall.question: A call booked 9:00–9:30 may run up to ten minutes over. When should the next task start so an overrun cannot collide?
recall.why: A gap absorbs delay up to its length; ten minutes of overrun needs a ten-minute gap, so 9:40.
